tasks.extracted: Point-of-care testing was done in two steps: 2–3 mg of the sample analysed by FTIR, then dissolved in water and tested with strips, with one combined result recorded; who read the strips and the water volume are not stated. Confirmatory samples came from five of the eight sites (three in Vancouver, two in Surrey). Second-hand: a report on similar strips (Shapiro et al., 2020) concluded that flualprazolam and flubromazolam were detected at concentrations similar to alprazolam, and etizolam at a higher minimum concentration that was still within the range useful for drug checking; the authors cite it as recent evidence of cross-reactivity supporting point-of-care use. The report was not read.
